newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine says has 252 mln tonnes proven oil reserve.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine says has 252 mln tonnes proven oil reserve.

text.p: Ukraine has 252 million tonnes of proven oil reserves and 1.2 trillion cubic metres of proven natural gas reserves, and has forecast rising output in both, the deputy head of the State Geology Committee said on Thursday.
Dmytro Hursky told a news conference that unproven reserves were higher than proven ones.
He did not say whether the reserves had been estimated according to international standards, which differ from Soviet-era standards still common in the region.
The government, in its three-year economic plan, planned to boost oil output to 4.8 million tonnes (96,000 barrels per day) in 2000 from 4.2 million tonnes (84,000 bpd) this year.

The State Oil and Gas Committee reported previously that Ukraine recovered 4.1 million tonnes of oil (82,000 bpd) last year, 0.2 percent more than in 1995, and 18.2 billion cubic metres of natural gas, 1.4 percent more than in 1995.
Natural gas recovery this year is forecast at 18.2 billion cubic metres, and 19 billion cubic metres in 2000.
The plan called for development of 105 new oil and natural gas sites this year, and according to government statistics 214 oil and natural gas sites are now being drilled.
